name: dsa-visualizer
description: Watch your C# solution run step by step, and see how its time and memory grow — built for learning data structures and algorithms.

dsaViz.enginePath.markdownDescription: Only for development: a different `DsaViz.Engine` executable to use. Leave empty — the extension uses the engine bundled inside it.

dsaViz.sizes.markdownDescription: Input sizes to measure. Leave empty to let the engine choose: it starts at `10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000` and drops to small sizes on its own when an algorithm is too expensive for them — which is the only way an exponential solution gets a curve at all.

dsaViz.timeoutSeconds.description: Longest a whole measurement may take before the engine is stopped. This is what guarantees the editor never waits forever.

dsaViz.budget.description: Maximum statements a single run may execute before it is stopped. This is what keeps a runaway loop from hanging the editor.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with DSA Visualizer
walkthroughs.description: Watch an algorithm run, then see why it has the complexity it has.

steps.title: Watch two pointers move
steps.description:
Open a two-pointer solution, then press **▶ Visualize** above `TwoSum`.
[Open Two Sum II](command:dsaViz.openSample?%5B%22TwoSumSorted.cs%22%5D)

steps.title: Try your own input on a tree
steps.description:
Open a breadth-first search, press **▶ Visualize**, then type a different tree in the box.
[Open Level Order Traversal](command:dsaViz.openSample?%5B%22LevelOrder.cs%22%5D)

steps.title: See why it's O(n)
steps.description:
Open a memoised dynamic-programming solution and press **Complexity**.
[Open Climbing Stairs](command:dsaViz.openSample?%5B%22ClimbStairs.cs%22%5D)
